simple.meaning: קָרִיא (qârîyʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “called , i.e. select.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קָרִיא (H7148) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 1:16, with occurrences in Numbers.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָרִיא (H7148) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קָרִיא (H7148) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קָרִיא (qârîyʼ) / H7148 is traced through Numbers 1:16, Numbers 16:2, Numbers 26:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

majorEvents.evidenceText: The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram who were called by the congregation, who rebelled against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah when they rebelled against Yahweh;

timeline.evidenceText: These are those who were called of the congregation, the princes† or, chiefs, or, leaders of the tribes of their fathers; they were the heads of the thousands of Israel.
